In this task, you will create a report on the penguins dataset using Quarto.

:::{.callout-tip}
Render your document often to check if everything still works. It's much easier to find mistakes if you render after every small change. Use the keyboard shortcut `Ctrl + Shift + K` (`Cmd + Shift + K` on Mac) to render quickly.
:::

## 1. Create a Quarto document

- Go to `File -> New File -> Quarto Document...`
- Use "Penguin Report" as title and choose the editor you prefer
- Render the document. RStudio asks you to save it first, e.g. as `penguin_report.qmd`
- Switch between the visual and the source editor to see the difference

## 2. Add Markdown text

Delete everything below the YAML header. Then write some words about the penguins dataset trying out some Markdown formatting:

- A section header (e.g. `## Introduction`)
- A sentence with **bold** and *italic* text
- A bullet list of the three penguin species
- A link to a website of your choice

Render the document.

## 3. Add code

- Add a code chunk that loads the `tidyverse`. Hide it completely with `#| include: false`
- Add another code chunk with a plot of the penguins data (e.g. a scatterplot or a boxplot). Hide the code with `#| echo: false` and the warnings with `#| warning: false`

Render the document. What is the difference between `include: false` and `echo: false`?

## 4. Add inline code

Write a sentence that includes the number of penguins in the data. Use inline code like this: `` `r knitr::inline_expr("nrow(penguins)")` ``

Render the document.

## 5. Extend the YAML header

Add an author and a date to the YAML header. Also add `execute` options to hide warnings and messages in all code chunks:

```yaml
---
title: "Penguin Report"
author: "Your Name"
date: today
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---
```

If your YAML header contains `editor: visual`, keep this line.

Render the document.

## For the fast ones

You can do these in any order, or skip them and just take a break.

### Explore the visual editor

Try the buttons and the `Insert` menu of the visual editor. Add for example an image, a table or a footnote.

### More markdown

Check the [Markdown reference](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html) and add anything you like to your document.

### More code

Add a code chunk that prints a summary table, e.g. the mean body mass of each species:

```{r}
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass, na.rm = TRUE), .by = species)
```

Try more chunk options for your plot, e.g. `#| fig-cap: "Your caption"`, `#| fig-align: center` or `#| out-width: "80%"`. You can find all options in the [code cell reference](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/cells/cells-knitr.html).

### More YAML options

Add more options to the YAML header, for example:

```yaml
---
title: "Penguin Report"
format: html
toc: true
number-sections: true
code-fold: true
---
```

You can find more options in the [HTML format reference](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html).

### Render to PDF or Word

Change `format: html` to `format: pdf` or `format: docx` and render.

For PDF, you may need to install LaTeX first. Run this in the R console:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# install.packages("tinytex") # only run this once
tinytex::install_tinytex() # only run this once
```
